title: The decompressor reports the buffer it allocated rather than the bytes it produced, so the reply carries whatever the heap held
index_line: T-0079 · MEM_READ · OP_COMPRESSED with an inflated uncompressedSize: allocation length used as produced length → heap bytes in the reply · cpp · corroborated
invariant_violated: The wire-protocol decompressor assumed a message's declared uncompressed size and the number of bytes zlib actually produced were interchangeable; returning the allocated size made the untouched tail look like valid BSON, so the parser walked uninitialised heap and the server shipped it back.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated client sends an OP_COMPRESSED wire message whose uncompressedSize field claims more bytes than the compressed payload will produce
the server allocates an output buffer sized from the attacker's claimed length
zlib inflates the real payload into the start of that buffer and leaves the remainder untouched
the decompressor hands on the allocated buffer size as the produced length, so the mismatch is never detected
BSON parsing walks the uninitialised tail as if it were field data, reading until it meets a NUL
those heap bytes are serialised into the reply document and returned to the unauthenticated client

source.protocol.value: the OP_COMPRESSED MongoDB wire message: a length field the client controls precedes any authentication

size.length.value: uncompressedSize (attacker-declared) versus the length zlib actually produced

sink.memory.copy.value: the decompression buffer allocation sized by the untrusted length; the untouched tail is later parsed as data

guard.none.value: no authentication is required to reach the decompressor, and no check compares produced length against the declaration

preconditions.expr: the mongod/mongos listener is reachable from the network
the server enables the zlib network compressor
the running build predates the fixed release for its branch

check.spec: mongod --version 2>/dev/null | head -3 || printf 'version check via buildInfo: '; curl -s http://HOST:27017/ | head -c 80

success: a reply document contains bytes the client never sent — kernel log lines, other sessions' data, or binary that is not valid BSON the client constructed
the leaked region tracks the inflated uncompressedSize the client chose
failure_like: the server rejects the message with a length/compat error
zlib compression is disabled (snappy/zstd-only), so this path is not compiled in
false_positive: a normal isMaster reply is not a leak — require bytes that are demonstrably foreign to the request
random-looking but zero-filled padding suggests an allocation artefact, not disclosure; verify the content is live heap data

hazards: every length-prefixed protocol with optional compression: the declared and produced lengths are two different numbers
the bug is pre-authentication because decompression happens before auth
the same accounting error becomes MEM_WRITE when the buffer is later written rather than parsed
non_transfers: implementations that size the buffer to the actual inflate output or memset the allocated region

provenance.author: MongoDB Server Engineering (SERVER-115508)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2025-14847: a client-side exploit of the server zlib implementation returns uninitialized heap memory without authenticating; workaround is disabling the zlib compressor; the linked fix commit is "Make minimally sized buffers for uncompressed Messages"

provenance.author: Joe Desimone (mongobleed PoC)
provenance.corroborates: independent mechanism analysis: the decompressor returns the allocated buffer size instead of the actual decompressed length; an inflated uncompressedSize makes the server allocate a large buffer, zlib fills only the start, and BSON parsing reads field names from the uninitialised tail until NUL bytes
